sara: Quick RFC follow-up: I posted the staged-delta watermark proposal here https://redwood.internal/rfcs/airgap-staged-delta
sara: TL;DR — use a monotonically increasing 'watermark' in manifests so operators can resume/verify partial applies and a lightweight inspector to detect whether a rollback is safe
sara: question: is the watermark enough for operator-initiated rollbacks, or do we need a richer rollback-inspector that inspects component activation state and reference counts?
ben: I skimmed — nice. My worry: operators will rely on watermark but disk/agent state can diverge (partial extract, powercut). Inspector seems necessary for safety checks
mike: +1 to an inspector. It can be conservative: if any component is mid-apply, refuse automated rollback and surface a guided playbook
katie: UX angle: we should avoid too many scary errors for operators. Suggest inspector produce a 3-tier outcome: green (safe), yellow (recommended manual steps), red (abort/forensics)
ben: agree on triage states. Also: what about cross-component dependencies? If component A rolled forward and B didn't, watermark alone doesn't encode dependency graph
sara: good catch. Current manifest has simple linear watermarks per component group, not whole-graph. We could add a small dependency matrix (hash refs) but want to keep bundle size small
mike: alternative: inspector validates activation graph by reading local activation markers (e.g., /var/lib/redwood/active-manifests/*) and verifying content hashes against bundle index
mike: pseudo-check:
```
for comp in manifest.components:
  if not file_exists(active_marker(comp)):
    state[comp] = "missing"
  elif hash(active_marker(comp)) != manifest.hash(comp):
    state[comp] = "mismatch"
  else:
    state[comp] = "ok"
```
katie: can we surface that as a single `redwood inspect-rollback --summary` call that outputs the triage and an ordered checklist for safe rollback?
sara: yes, plan was to add an `inspect-rollback` endpoint to the operator agent that returns JSON (but for Slack thread we care about UX that operators see)
ben: security: inspector needs to run unprivileged and not change state. Read-only. Good to mention that in RFC
mike: also consider signature timelines. If we let rollbacks re-apply older manifests, audit needs to include signer/time and optionally KMS reapproval for older artifacts
sara: RFC currently suggests signed manifest bundles with a signer chain and timestamp. Inspector should include signature verification and report signer identity
katie: UI: show signer, timestamp, and whether signer key is still trusted (revocation list check)
ben: operational edge-case: partial delta where new artifacts were cleaned up by GC but watermark advanced. Inspector must detect missing blobs and either fetch from fallback seed or refuse
sara: yes — propose a fallback-seed tier in the agent config: `fallback_seeds: [s3://seed1, file:///mnt/seed2]` used only for verification/rollback (no autopull in strict airgap mode unless operator enables)
mike: that keeps airgap guarantees intact. We should make autopull opt-in via operator flag `allow_fallback_fetch` with clear warnings
katie: can we add a small human-readable playbook in the manifest for yellow-state remediation? Eg a short list of steps keyed by component name
sara: we can embed a 1-3 line `remediation_hint` per component in the manifest. Lightweight and helpful
ben: performance: inspector should avoid scanning full blobs. Use component-level markers + stored hashes. Full blob verification only when requested (`--deep`)
mike: agree. Also rate-limit deep checks and surface ETA
ops-bot: deploy-bot: RFC comment period ends in 5d — please leave final design notes
sara: actionable items from thread:
- add triage states (green/yellow/red) to the RFC
- define inspector read-only API and example `inspect-rollback` output
- add signer/timestamp checks and revocation policy note
- add fallback_seed config + opt-in flag
- include remediation_hint field in manifest schema
katie: I'll draft the UX example for `inspect-rollback --summary` and a sample checklist
ben: I'll add the revocation and GC edge-case section
mike: I'll prototype inspector pseudo-code and a shallow verification mode
sara: thanks all — I'll update the RFC today and ping you when done :thumbsup:
ops-bot: note: RFC updated to include triage states and remediation_hint (automated update)"
